title: Israeli airstrike destroys Iranian consular building in Damascus
body:
On 1 April 2024, at about 17:00 local time, an airstrike attributed to Israel destroyed the consular section of the Iranian Embassy in the Mezzeh district of Damascus, Syria. Iranian Major General Mohammad Reza Zahedi, a senior commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), was among those killed.

Reports of the toll varied. Al Jazeera later cited 13 dead, including Zahedi and six other Iranian nationals as well as at least six Syrian citizens. A tally compiled in the Wikipedia article on the strike lists 16 killed: seven IRGC officers, five Iran-backed militiamen, one Hezbollah member, one Iranian adviser and two Syrian civilians.

Israel did not immediately comment on the strike. Iran described the targeted building as part of its diplomatic mission, while the Israeli position was that the site was a military facility used by the IRGC. The strike became the stated reason for Iran's drone and missile attack on Israel on 13 and 14 April 2024, which Iran said was retaliation for the Damascus attack. It was one of several escalations between Israel and Iran and its allies that year, alongside the continuing cross-border exchanges between Israel and Hezbollah, and it prompted wide international concern about a regional war.
